name: Discovery Question Types
description: Question categories available to Discovery conversations. These describe purpose and usage only, not prompt text.

types.name: Narrative Questions
types.purpose: Invite stories, context, self-description, and participant language.
types.description: Questions that help the participant explain themselves through lived examples.
types.usageGuidance: Use early and whenever participant story is more useful than direct abstraction.

types.name: Reflective Questions
types.purpose: Help the participant notice meaning, themes, and self-understanding.
types.description: Questions that invite the participant to consider what their examples reveal.
types.usageGuidance: Use after evidence has emerged, not before the participant has had room to explore.

types.name: Exploration Questions
types.purpose: Broaden or deepen an area of interest, energy, uncertainty, or significance.
types.description: Questions that open additional terrain without forcing a fixed path.
types.usageGuidance: Use when a domain is promising, unclear, emotionally significant, or participant-led.

types.name: Evidence Questions
types.purpose: Ground observations in examples, transcript segments, and participant statements.
types.description: Questions that ask for situations, examples, or moments that support an emerging observation.
types.usageGuidance: Use when an insight is plausible but not yet sufficiently supported.

types.name: Clarifying Questions
types.purpose: Resolve ambiguity without narrowing the participant too quickly.
types.description: Questions that distinguish meaning, context, or intent.
types.usageGuidance: Use sparingly when confusion would otherwise distort understanding.

types.name: Future Questions
types.purpose: Explore desired direction, growth, values, and possible alignment without making recommendations.
types.description: Questions that help reveal aspiration and opportunity signals.
types.usageGuidance: Use after enough present or past context exists to avoid speculative profiling.

types.name: Tension Questions
types.purpose: Explore competing desires, contradictions, and unresolved priorities.
types.description: Questions that preserve complexity rather than resolve it.
types.usageGuidance: Use when two participant truths appear to coexist in meaningful tension.
